_why: The registry's whole job is to notice a wire disappearing, and for one record it did the disappearing itself: keyed on the bare `id`, `register` upserted one feature's Task 4 over another's and `compare` — keyed the same way — saw the successor and reported nothing. Every mutation here restores the bare-id key at one of the four places it lives, because the defect was not a missing check but an identity that was one field too small, and each spelling of it fails silently in the same direction: a real removal reads as no removal at all.

mutations.name: identity-drops-the-owning-feature
mutations._mechanism: The defect at its source. Every consumer keeps calling the right helper and the helper answers with the wrong identity, so registration, comparison and the halt reasons all regress together — which is exactly why the key is one function rather than four expressions.

mutations.name: register-upserts-on-the-bare-id-again
mutations._mechanism: The original line, restored verbatim. A second feature's Task 4 evicts the first, and nothing anywhere reports it -- no tombstone, no provenance, no halt. This is the write that lost `audit-cycle-verb :: Task 4`.

mutations.name: compare-masks-a-removal-behind-the-same-id
mutations._mechanism: The half that made the loss invisible rather than merely destructive. With the successor occupying the id, the evicted record is 'present at HEAD' and `step5f:undeclared_removal` structurally cannot fire — a guard reporting PASS about a wire it can no longer see.
mutations.find:
head_keys = {_record_key(record) for record in head_records}
    return [record for record in base_records if _record_key(record) not in head_keys]
mutations.replace:
head_ids = {record["id"] for record in head_records}
    return [record for record in base_records if record["id"] not in head_ids]

mutations.name: halt-reason-names-no-single-wire
mutations._mechanism: Once two features may each own a `Task 4`, `step5f:undeclared_removal:Task 4` identifies neither of them, and two simultaneous removals emit the same line twice. The verdict stays correct while the remedy becomes unactionable, which is the failure mode a halt reason exists to prevent.

mutations.name: documented-contract-drifts-from-the-emitted-one
mutations._mechanism: SKILL.md is the contract 5f is run from. The fidelity test scrapes the emitted f-strings and diffs them against the documented tokens, so a halt reason that changes shape without the doc following it is caught here rather than by an operator grepping for a string the code no longer prints.
